reviews.rationale: Sequential GAAP comparison of selected rows shows modestly higher net interest income, higher noninterest income, and slightly higher noninterest expense and credit loss provision, leaving pretax and net income to common higher and diluted EPS higher on a GAAP basis. The FTE net interest margin is essentially flat, so the net interest income increase is not attributable to margin expansion in these rows. The provision increase offsets most of the net interest income increase at the after-provision line, so the profit improvement is better described as driven by noninterest income than by core spread economics. All comparisons are sequential, not year over year; GAAP and non-GAAP bases are kept separate; no guidance or realized-versus-guided comparison is available in this extract. Signed accounting bridges are identities, not causal explanations, and no source-backed driver facts are stored, so causal attribution remains unresolved. The thesis is a source-bounded monitoring record with no valuation conclusion, so the research state is maintained rather than upgraded.
